purpose: Non-windowed verification of Rust tab/pin menu composition, stable target resolution, typed split/tab actions and drop geometry; native UI acceptance deferred
build_consistency: final Ninja dry run reported no work to do
unit_verified_mechanisms: Rust composes the established menu order, command IDs and Polish labels for paired/unpaired targets, both split orientations and HTTP eligibility. Native URL/rule semantics are represented only by an eligibility flag.

Opaque 128-bit page identities resolve to the current tab index after reindexing. Removed identities are rejected even when a new page occupies their old index; foreign/empty source workspaces, ambiguous targets, missing pins and folders are rejected.
Typed menu actions revalidate readiness, busy state, current target, split side/membership and last-tab close protection. The side-to-move policy follows pane order independently of orientation.

The existing physical right-half drop target uses inclusive center/upper/left boundaries and exclusive lower/right boundaries. Empty bounds and disallowed targets are rejected; widened arithmetic avoids coordinate overflow.
implemented_pending_runtime_verification: The native ShellTab data adapter carries the full WebContents unique token as two 64-bit integers. Metadata updates do not format an identity string; cached row structure comparisons include page identity so replacement pages receive new callbacks.

The Metal backend builds SimpleMenuModel from the Rust command/label plan. Native View-to-item lookup and popup presentation remain adapters. Existing application command IDs have a compile-time assertion against the Rust plan contract.

Tab/split menu dispatch captures workspace, stable page identity or pin ID. At posted-task execution, Rust resolves the live target and returns a typed action; native callbacks still perform browser/profile operations.

Cached row drop callbacks retain their source workspace and stable target. Rust resolves the target and drop geometry before queueing, and split tasks resolve it again before invoking application callbacks.
The default Views menu plan and positional command route remain for comparison. Source-workspace capture also protects its cached drop callbacks from applying to a different active workspace.

The compiled regression builds models without opening a popup, but its browser fixture still opens a window; it is unrun under the no-window policy. It covers queued close after index shift, removed/replaced identities, foreign-workspace split rejection, split-side enablement and vertical labels.
deferred_checkpoint: Run the curated 46-case Metal matrix (the prior 45 plus RowMenuPlansAndQueuedIdentitySurviveReindex) and all 17 Views controls against these rebuilt sources.
Inspect native popup selection/dismissal, keyboard/AX invocation, split-pane menus, tab/pin drag-to-split at width/edge limits, cancelled drags, collapsed folders and busy/profile transitions.

Verify actual queued-command identity behavior after close/reorder/replace/workspace changes, last-tab rules, pin targets and profile/session isolation. Include the previous animation/palette regressions.
Package/sign and inspect the matching isolated app; measure real CPU/GPU/presentation workload and large-sidebar menu behavior separately.
limitations: Compilation and unit tests do not prove native menu/drag integration, persistence, AX/focus behavior or performance. Browser tests and app inspection remain unaccepted until the checkpoint.

Native popup and View identity/event nodes, link/rule services and application callbacks remain. Closing through other native controls is outside this menu-dispatch migration; full UI migration is incomplete.

This stage adds no dependency, crate or framework. Chromium page-token and existing base/standard-library types are already available. Original-code Apache-2.0 and required upstream notices are unchanged.
